newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Astra says US 9 mo Losec sales up 37 pct.
newsitem.headline: Astra says US 9 mo Losec sales up 37 pct.

text.p: Swedish drugs company Astra AB said on Wednesday that sales of its ulcer treatment drug Losec in the U.S. rose 37 percent in the first nine months of 1996 against a year ago to $1.22 billion.
Astra said in a statement sales of the drug, which is known as Prilosec in the U.S., were affected to some extent by changes in wholesale inventories.
"Adjusted for these changes, sales growth for Prilosec was approximately 40 percent during the period January to September 1996," Astra said.
Astra spokesman Staffan Ternby told Reuters there had been no major changes in U.S. Losec sales in the third quarter as a result of inventory changes.
Sales of hypertension and angina treatment Plendil in the U.S. amounted to $55 million during the period, the company said, compared with $50 million in the corresponding 1995 period.

Astra's products are marketed in the U.S. through Astra Merck Inc, which is equally owned by Astra and American drugs groups Merck & Co. Half of Astra Merck's sales are included in the sales of each parent company.
